content.question_text: What term is used when you supply a new method in a subclass because the superclass method is not appropriate?

core_requirements: Overriding (or to override) the superclass method.

content.question_text: Can a subclass method directly access the private fields of its superclass? If not, how must it access that data?

core_requirements: No, it cannot directly access the private fields.
It must use the public interface (the public methods) of the superclass.
acceptable_variations: No, it has to call a public getter method from the parent.

content.question_text: What happens if a subclass method tries to call the superclass version of the method by just using its name (e.g., `getSalary()` calling `getSalary()`)?

core_requirements: This creates an infinite chain of calls leading to a program crash.
acceptable_variations: Infinite loop/recursion that crashes the program.

content.question_text: What special keyword must you use to indicate that you want to call a method of the superclass, rather than the current class?
Why is it inaccurate to think of the `super` keyword as being completely analogous to the `this` reference?

core_requirements: `super` is not a reference to an object.
You cannot assign the value `super` to another object variable; it is only a special keyword directing the compiler.
acceptable_variations: Unlike 'this', 'super' isn't an actual object reference and can't be assigned to a variable.

content.question_text: Can inheritance take away fields or methods from a superclass?

core_requirements: Inheritance can never take away any fields or methods.
